clauses.heading: Abstract
sentences: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 provides guidance to industry, government agencies, and other organizations to manage cybersecurity risks.
This document describes CSF 2.0, its components, and some of the many ways that it can be used.

clauses.heading: Keywords
sentences: cybersecurity;
Cybersecurity Framework (CSF); cybersecurity risk governance; cybersecurity risk management; enterprise risk management;

clauses.heading: Audience
sentences: Individuals responsible for developing and leading cybersecurity programs are the primary audience for the CSF.

Additionally, the CSF can be useful to those making and influencing policy (e.g., associations, professional organizations, regulators) who set and communicate priorities for cybersecurity risk management.

clauses.heading: Supplemental Content
sentences: NIST will continue to build and host additional resources to help organizations implement the CSF, including Quick Start Guides and Community Profiles.
Suggestions for additional resources to reference on the NIST CSF website can always be shared with NIST at cyberframework@nist.gov.

clauses.heading: Note to Readers
sentences: Unless otherwise noted, documents cited, referenced, or excerpted in this publication are not wholly incorporated into this publication.

Before version 2.0, the Cybersecurity Framework was called the “Framework for Improving Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity.” This title is not used for CSF 2.0. i NIST CSWP 29 The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

clauses.heading: Acknowledgments
sentences: The CSF is the result of a multi-year collaborative effort across industry, academia, and government in the United States and around the world.

clauses.heading: Preface
sentences: The Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 is designed to help organizations of all sizes and sectors — including industry, government, academia, and nonprofit — to manage and reduce their cybersecurity risks.
The CSF is designed to be valuable for any type of organization and is expected to provide appropriate guidance over a long time. iv NIST CSWP 29 The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

clauses.heading: Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) Overview
sentences: Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) Overview This document is version 2.0 of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (Framework or CSF).
NIST CSWP 29 The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

clauses.heading: Introduction to the CSF Core
sentences: Introduction to the CSF Core Appendix A is the CSF Core — a set of cybersecurity outcomes arranged by Function, then Category, and finally Subcategory, as depicted in Fig. 1.
NIST CSWP 29 The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

clauses.heading: Introduction to CSF Profiles and Tiers
sentences: Introduction to CSF Profiles and Tiers This section defines the concepts of CSF Profiles and Tiers.

children.heading: CSF Profiles
sentences: CSF Profiles A CSF Organizational Profile describes an organization’s current and/or target cybersecurity posture in terms of the Core’s outcomes.

Also, a Target Profile can help express the organization’s cybersecurity risk management requirements and expectations to suppliers, partners, and other third parties as a target for those parties to achieve.

children.heading: CSF Tiers
sentences: CSF Tiers An organization can choose to use the Tiers to inform its Current and Target Profiles.
NIST CSWP 29 The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

clauses.heading: Introduction to Online Resources That Supplement the CSF
sentences: Introduction to Online Resources That Supplement the CSF NIST and other organizations have produced a suite of online resources that help organizations understand, adopt, and use the CSF.
NIST CSWP 29 The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

clauses.heading: Improving Cybersecurity Risk Communication and Integration
sentences: Improving Cybersecurity Risk Communication and Integration The CSF’s use will vary based on an organization’s unique mission and risks.

The selected outcomes can be used to focus on and implement strategic decisions to improve cybersecurity postures and maintain continuity of mission- essential functions while taking priorities and available resources into account.

children.heading: Improving Risk Management Communication
sentences: Improving Risk Management Communication The CSF provides a basis for improved communication regarding cybersecurity expectations, planning, and resources.
Updates to expectations and priorities are included in updated Organizational Profiles as the cycle repeats.

children.heading: Improving Integration with Other Risk Management Programs
sentences: Improving Integration with Other Risk Management Programs Every organization faces numerous types of ICT risk (e.g., privacy, supply chain, artificial intelligence) and may use frameworks and management tools that are specific to each risk.
NIST CSWP 29 The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

children.heading: CSF Category
sentences: A group of related cybersecurity outcomes that collectively comprise a CSF Function.

children.heading: CSF Community Profile
sentences: A baseline of CSF outcomes that is created and published to address shared interests and goals among a number of organizations.
An organization can use a Community Profile as the basis for its own Target Profile.

children.heading: CSF Core
sentences: A taxonomy of high-level cybersecurity outcomes that can help any organization manage its cybersecurity risks.
Its components are a hierarchy of Functions, Categories, and Subcategories that detail each outcome.

children.heading: CSF Current Profile
sentences: A part of an Organizational Profile that specifies the Core outcomes that an organization is currently achieving (or attempting to achieve) and characterizes how or to what extent each outcome is being achieved.

children.heading: CSF Function
sentences: The highest level of organization for cybersecurity outcomes.
There are six CSF Functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, and Recover.

children.heading: CSF Implementation Example
sentences: A concise, action-oriented, notional illustration of a way to help achieve a CSF Core outcome.

children.heading: CSF Informative Reference
sentences: A mapping that indicates a relationship between a CSF Core outcome and an existing standard, guideline, regulation, or other content.

children.heading: CSF Organizational Profile
sentences: A mechanism for describing an organization’s current and/or target cybersecurity posture in terms of the CSF Core’s outcomes.

children.heading: CSF Quick Start Guide
sentences: A supplementary resource that gives brief, actionable guidance on specific CSF-related topics.

children.heading: CSF Subcategory
sentences: A group of more specific outcomes of technical and management cybersecurity activities that comprise a CSF Category.

children.heading: CSF Target Profile
sentences: A part of an Organizational Profile that specifies the desired Core outcomes that an organization has selected and prioritized for achieving its cybersecurity risk management objectives.

children.heading: CSF Tier
sentences: A characterization of the rigor of an organization’s cybersecurity risk governance and management practices.
